assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: bug (known_failing — ModelName is full; ContextWindow is not reachable today)
driver_capability: gap:settings_model

Route: driver-gap. This is NOT a frozen cell — a real Go adapter exists and is green (`go test ./core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/... -race -count=1` passes today), so this assessment is the opposite of the earlier circular 'frozen, no Go adapter' verdicts: the agent, transcript, and parser all genuinely exist and were exercised live.

## agent_supports — yes (live-verified twice)

`muse --help` documents a top-level `--model <MODEL>` flag ('Model id for non-echo providers'). I drove this LIVE on this machine (not just read the flag): `muse --trust-workspace --model muse-spark-1.2` launched with the composer footer reading `muse-spark-1.2 · high · <cwd>` (the DEFAULT model on this account/session is `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` — confirmed both in the same probe session before the pin, and in muse-format-spec.md §7's corpus evidence — so this is a genuine non-default launch, not an echo of the default). A follow-up 'reply with exactly: ok' turn completed normally.

Separately, I confirmed the in-REPL `/model` slash command is NOT usable as an inline-argument command: launching fresh and sending `/model muse-spark-1.2` as one line (text + Enter) opened the SAME arrow-key picker as a bare `/model` — the picker ignores trailing text entirely; it never applies the typed id. `Escape` closes it back to the composer with the model UNCHANGED. This means the only reliable way to pin a non-default model is the CLI launch flag, not an in-REPL command (relevant to the driver pillar below, and to sibling scenario 5.3 model-switch-midsession, not assessed here).

## daemon_capability — bug (ModelName full; ContextWindow known_failing)

**ModelName: full.** `core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/parser.go`'s `parseRunModelConfigured` (payload_type `run.model.configured`, fires once per run) reads `record.model_id` and sets `ev.ModelName`; `parseMetadata` (`runtime.session.metadata`) and `parseModelCompleted` (`model_completed.model`) both also set it as backup/confirmation sources. Live-verified end-to-end through the PRODUCTION code, not just by reading source: I ran `tailer.NewTranscriptTailer(path, &muse.Parser{}, muse.AdapterName).TailAndProcess()` (a `go run` probe, the same call `parser_test.go`/`metrics_test.go` use) against my live-captured session.jsonl and got `ModelName="muse-spark-1.2"` — the pinned launch model, never 'unknown'. The transcript itself carries three independent, mutually consistent records: `runtime.session.metadata.record.model_id="muse-spark-1.2"`, `run.model.configured{model_id:"muse-spark-1.2",source:"startup"}`, and `model_completed.model="muse-spark-1.2"`.

One correction to muse-format-spec.md §7's framing: that doc describes `runtime.model_reconfigure.completed` as firing 'once at session start' alongside `run.model.configured`. My live probe with an EXPLICIT `--model` flag shows only `run.model.configured{source:"startup"}` — no `runtime.model_reconfigure.completed` at all. Re-reading §7's own quoted example, that event's `previous.model_id` is EMPTY (`""`) — it fires only when resolving an unset default, not when a flag pins the model directly. Doesn't change the verdict (parseModelReconfigure is a redundant backup source, never the only one), but the spec's 'fires once at session start' description is incomplete without this distinction.

**ContextWindow: known_failing, two independent, stacked causes:**

1. **A genuine parser defect** (fixable, in-our-control): `parseModelCompleted` (parser.go lines 371-422) reads `usage.input_tokens`/`usage.output_tokens` into a local `bd tailer.UsageBreakdown` and forwards it via `ev.Contribution` (for cumulative cost/token accounting — this part works, see below) — but the `ev.Tokens = &tailer.TokenSnapshot{...}` literal at lines 415-420 sets `Input`/`Output`/`CacheRead`/`CacheCreation` and OMITS `.Total`. `core/pkg/tailer/tailer_metrics.go`'s `applyTokenSnapshot` (line ~296-303) only copies into `SessionMetrics.TotalTokens` when `tokens.Total > 0` — so `TotalTokens` stays 0 for every muse session, always, regardless of real usage. `computeContextUtilization` (tailer_metrics.go:761-777) short-circuits at `if t.metrics.TotalTokens == 0 || t.metrics.ModelName == "" { ...; return }` BEFORE it ever calls into the capacity manager, so ContextWindow can never be resolved by this path for ANY muse session today. This is unlike junie/copilot/vibe, which all populate `.Total` from some source (junie: a dedicated context-report event OR `Total: used`; copilot/vibe: `Total: <cumulative-or-turn total>`) — muse's parser has the exact same ingredients (`bd.Input`/`bd.Output`) sitting in the SAME function, just never copied across.

   Live-reproduced, not just source-read: my `go run` probe against the live-captured transcript printed `ContextWindow=0 ContextWindowUnknown=false TotalTokens=0` alongside `CumInputTokens=28577 CumOutputTokens=173` (proving the usage data DID flow through `parseModelCompleted` into `Contribution`/cum-token accumulation — the capacity-manager log line `no pricing for model "muse-spark-1.2"` even fired, proving `ModelName` and `Contribution` both reached the cost-pricing attempt) while `Tokens`/`TotalTokens` stayed at their zero value the whole time.

2. **A separate, external, non-code gap** (same class as mistral-vibe's own 5.2 cell caveat): even a hypothetical `.Total` fix would not be sufficient — `core/pkg/capacity`'s LiteLLM-derived table and `core/pkg/capacity/aliases.go` have zero entries for `muse`/`spark`/any Meta-internal model family (confirmed: `git grep -in muse core/pkg/capacity/aliases.go` — zero hits; the capacity cache JSON fixtures in this repo also carry no muse/spark keys). `capacity.GetModelCapacity` returns a zero-value `ModelCapacity` for an unrecognized name (confirmed by reading `capacity.go:101-112` — no sentinel/fallback window exists anywhere in this codebase, confirmed by an empty grep for `32000`/`sentinel` across `core/pkg/tailer` and `core/pkg/capacity`). So `effectiveContextWindow <= 0` even after a `.Total` fix, and `ComputeContextUtilization` returns `(0, 0, "unknown", true)`.

   Fix #1 alone is necessary-but-not-sufficient; both need to land (the parser defect is a daemon-side bug worth its own fix regardless of pricing-catalog status — it also silently disables ContextWindow/pressure-level display and `ContextWindowUnknown`'s accuracy for EVERY muse session, not just this cell's pinned-model case) before 'ContextWindow matches the model's published window' can ever pass for muse. This is why the verdict is `bug`, not `full`-with-caveat: mistral-vibe's own 5.2 cell (replaydata/agents/mistral-vibe/scenarios/5-2_model-identification) stayed `daemon=full` because ITS blocker is #2 alone (its parser DOES wire `.Total`/`ContextWindow` correctly, from `sidecar.go`'s `st.contextTokens`/`st.contextWindow`) — muse additionally has #1, a genuine code-level omission the daemon COULD reasonably handle.

**Tokens (the OTHER, working accounting path) and cost: unaffected, confirmed live.** `Contribution`-based cumulative accounting (`CumInputTokens`/`CumOutputTokens`, feeding `tokens_nonzero` in `observations`) is a SEPARATE mechanism from the `Tokens`/`TotalTokens`/ContextWindow one, and it DOES work: my probe read `CumInputTokens=28577 CumOutputTokens=173` off the same transcript — matches the already-committed 5-1_token-accounting cell's independent verdict (`daemon_capability: full`) for that mechanism. `cost_nonzero` is correctly `false` for the same reason as gap #2 above (no pricing entry) — NOT a defect, per the evidence brief's own explicit instruction that 'no dollar cost is persisted anywhere' is expected/by-design, verified by a strict JSON-key scan (muse-format-spec.md §6).

## driver_capability — gap:settings_model

The interactive driver's step-type vocabulary (`DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash wait_turn sleep exit_clean"`, replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh:139) fully covers this recipe's needed steps (send/wait_turn/sleep/exit_clean) — recipe-lint's grammar+semantic checks pass clean with zero step-type gap.

But launching with a NON-DEFAULT model needs the CLI `--model <id>` flag (the only reliable path — the in-REPL `/model` command always opens a `keys`-driven picker, live-confirmed above, and `keys` is an unimplemented stub: `keys) not_implemented keys` at driver-interactive.sh:453), and `launch_repl()` (driver-interactive.sh:226-258) hardcodes `tmux new-session ... "muse" --trust-workspace` with NO read of `$SETTINGS_PATH` at all — confirmed by `grep -n SETTINGS_PATH replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh`, which returns exactly one hit, the parameter's own declaration at line 83 (`SETTINGS_PATH="$4"   # scenario settings blob; wire into the launch if the agent reads one` — the comment itself says it currently is not read).

This is the SAME class of missing seam kiro-cli's driver closed under #599 ('the driver's settings.model knob... appends --model <m> at launch, mirroring the trust_all_tools seam' — replaydata/agents/kiro-cli/driver-interactive.sh:107-111,291 reads `.model` from `$SETTINGS_PATH` and appends `--model $MODEL` to its launch command). `record` should port the identical pattern into muse's `launch_repl()`.

**Vacuous-pass mitigation, not just a note:** if `record` records this cell WITHOUT wiring the settings.model knob, the driver silently launches with the DEFAULT model (`muse-spark-1.3-contributor`) instead of the pinned one — which is STILL non-empty/non-'unknown', so a spec that only asserted 'ModelName != unknown' would falsely pass without ever having launched a non-default model at all. The spec below defends against exactly this by asserting `observations.model` as an EXACT match on `"muse-spark-1.2"` (the pinned id), not merely non-'unknown' — a driver that never wires the launch flag will correctly FAIL this assertion (surfacing the still-open gap) instead of silently passing.

## What irrlicht does NOT see (out of scope / already covered elsewhere)

- Mid-session model switching (`/model` picker navigation) is scenario 5.3 model-switch-midsession, not assessed here — the picker's `keys` gap is a real driver blocker for THAT scenario, not this one (this cell only needs a launch-time pin).
- Context-window CAPACITY resolution once both blockers above are fixed is still gated on a `core/pkg/capacity` catalog/alias entry for muse's models existing at all — an ongoing maintenance concern (`/ir:refresh-aliases`-style), not something this adapter's code can solve unilaterally.
- session-index.db is confirmed (muse-format-spec.md §6, and this adapter's own package doc) to carry no token/model columns reliably enough to use as a fallback source; not relevant to this cell's blockers.
caveats: known_failing: ContextWindow will read 0 (ContextWindowUnknown initially false, since the totalTokens==0 early return in ComputeContextUtilization never reaches the unknown=true branch) for every muse recording today, due to TWO independent, stacked gaps: (1) core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/parser.go:415-420 never sets tailer.TokenSnapshot.Total in parseModelCompleted (a genuine, fixable parser omission — live-reproduced via a go run probe against a real captured transcript: ModelName/CumInputTokens/CumOutputTokens all populated correctly while TotalTokens/ContextWindow stayed zero), and (2) core/pkg/capacity has no pricing/context-window entry for any muse-spark-* model (confirmed via git grep and the live 'no pricing for model' log line), so even a #1 fix alone is not sufficient. Filing an issue for #1 is record's job once it reproduces this live per the assess SKILL's daemon=bug protocol; I did not open one (assess does not file issues, and 'never open an issue nobody asked for').

Vacuous-pass check: this cell would pass while proving nothing about a NON-DEFAULT launch if the driver's settings.model knob is left unwired and the recorded session silently launches with the account default (muse-spark-1.3-contributor) instead of the pinned muse-spark-1.2 — ModelName would still read non-'unknown', which a loose spec could mistake for success. Mitigated by asserting observations.model as an EXACT match on the pinned id ("muse-spark-1.2"), not merely non-empty, so an unwired driver fails this assertion loudly instead of passing hollow.

Load-bearing environment precondition (carried from the sibling 2-1_basic-turn cell, unchanged): --trust-workspace is required on every launch because every staging cwd is freshly created; without it muse's untrusted-workspace modal silently eats the first send (muse-driver-audit.md defect #1, live-reproduced).

muse-spark-1.2 was chosen as the pinned model because it is a real, currently-selectable option in the live account's own /model picker enumeration (muse-spark-1.3, muse-spark-1.3-contributor [default], muse-spark-1.2, muse-spark-1.2-contributor) and was live-launch-verified on this machine — not a doc-guessed name. This is account/tier-scoped (same caveat the 2-1_basic-turn cell raises about '-contributor' reading as account-scoped), so a different account's picker enumeration is UNVERIFIED to carry the identical four options; record should re-probe --list-models-equivalent (muse has no explicit --list-models flag; the picker itself is the enumeration surface) if the pin ever fails to launch on a different account.

cost_nonzero is asserted false, not true, per the evidence brief and muse-format-spec.md §6's strict JSON-key scan: no dollar-cost field is ever persisted by muse, by design (client-side pricing computation is the norm for every adapter) — not a defect in this cell.

This assessment's live probes (tmux drive + go run tailer probe) used --provider meta against a live authenticated account, not --provider echo — --provider echo was tried first and confirmed unusable for model selection ('model selection is not available for this session'), so it is not a viable low-cost substitute for this specific scenario.

The reference pattern to port: reads .model from $SETTINGS_PATH and appends --model $MODEL to the launch command.

This repo's own precedent for scoping model-identification's ContextWindow criterion around a pricing-catalog gap while keeping daemon=full — cited here to explain why muse's verdict differs (muse additionally has a genuine parser-code omission, not only a pricing-catalog gap).

Sibling cells confirming the Contribution/Cum* token-accounting path is independently daemon=full, and the house recipe style (send 'Reply with exactly the word: ok' / wait_turn / sleep / exit_clean, --trust-workspace precondition) this cell's recipe mirrors.

preconditions: muse CLI installed and on PATH, v1.2.1 (muse --version >= 1.2.1 per replaydata/agents/muse/metadata.json)
muse auth complete: 'muse login' (Meta account, browser code approval) or META_API_KEY exported -- auth is set up out-of-band, the rig's precheck delegates it to the user
tmux available -- the interactive driver runs muse in a tmux REPL
irrlichd is recording -- either run-cell.sh in isolated mode, or --attach against a running daemon started with --record

DRIVER WORK REQUIRED before this cell can genuinely record a non-default model: replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh's launch_repl() must read settings.model from $SETTINGS_PATH and append `--model <id>` to the muse launch command (port kiro-cli's driver-interactive.sh:88-111,291 pattern). Without this, the recipe below launches the account DEFAULT model instead of the pinned one -- see the assessment's vacuous-pass caveat.

muse-spark-1.2 (the pinned model below) is a live-confirmed selectable option on this machine's account; a different account may enumerate different /model picker options -- re-verify with a fresh `muse --model <id> --trust-workspace` dry launch if this pin ever fails.
setup: Driver launches `muse --trust-workspace --model muse-spark-1.2` (once the settings.model knob above is ported) in a fresh per-run cwd under a tmux session, mirroring 2-1_basic-turn's launch shape

The in-REPL `/model` slash command is deliberately NOT used to pin the model -- live-confirmed it always opens an arrow-key picker (even with an inline argument like `/model muse-spark-1.2`, which is silently ignored), and picker navigation needs the driver's unimplemented `keys` step
One no-tool turn is enough to elicit run.model.configured + model_completed with the pinned model id; ModelName/token assertions are checked AFTER turn_end
ContextWindow/context-utilization assertions are EXPECTED TO FAIL today (known_failing) -- see the assessment's daemon_capability=bug reasoning; do not weaken these assertions to match the bug

script.text: Reply with exactly the word: ok

verify: events.jsonl shows one ready -> working -> ready cycle, single-birth (session id = the session directory basename), no waiting, no tool-call event
after turn_end, SessionMetrics.ModelName = 'muse-spark-1.2' (the pinned launch model) -- NOT the account default 'muse-spark-1.3-contributor', NOT 'unknown'

KNOWN FAILING today: SessionMetrics.ContextWindow > 0 / matches muse-spark-1.2's published window -- currently always 0 (see assessment). This assertion stays in the spec (never weakened) so record's verify surfaces the gap instead of hiding it.
cost stays 0 (no litellm pricing entry for muse-spark-1.2) -- expected, not a defect
final session state is ready before exit_clean tears the REPL down
